audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph supporters joining David at Ziklag and Hebron, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for defectors and divided loyalties, Benjaminite kin of Saul, animalized warrior imagery, river crossing and valley flight, betrayal fears, spirit speech, Philistine rejection, raider conflict, troop census, command hierarchy, Issachar time-discernment, unity rhetoric, and food logistics.

modern.text: And David went out to meet them, saying, “If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my enemies when my hands are free of violence, may the God of our fathers see it and judge you.”

modern.text: Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, the chief of the Thirty, and he said: “We are yours, O David! We are with you, O son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, for your God helps you.” So David received them and made them leaders of his troops.

modern.text: Some from Manasseh defected to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul. (They did not help the Philistines because the Philistine rulers consulted and sent David away, saying, “It will cost us our heads if he defects to his master Saul.”)

familiar.text: And of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valour, famous throughout the house of their fathers.

modern.text: From Ephraim: 20,800 mighty men of valor, famous among their own clans.

original.text: וּמִן בְּנֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וּשְׁמוֹנֶ֣ה מֵא֑וֹת גִּבּ֣וֹרֵי חַ֔יִל אַנְשֵׁ֥י שֵׁמ֖וֹת לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָֽם

verses.restored: From half-tribe Manasseh: eighteen thousand named to come make David king.

familiar.text: And of the half tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, which were expressed by name, to come and make David king.

modern.text: From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000 designated by name to come and make David king.

original.text: וּמֵחֲצִי֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אָ֑לֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִקְּבוּ֙ בְּשֵׁמ֔וֹת לָב֖וֹא לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת דָּוִֽיד

verses.restored: From Issachar, people understanding times and knowing what Israel should do: two hundred heads, and all relatives under their command.

familiar.text: And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.

modern.text: From Issachar, men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: 200 chiefs with all their kinsmen at their command.

original.text: וּמִבְּנֵ֣י יִשָּׂשכָ֗ר יוֹדְעֵ֤י בִינָה֙ לַֽעִתִּ֔ים לָדַ֖עַת מַה יַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רָאשֵׁיהֶ֣ם מָאתַ֔יִם וְכָל אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם עַל פִּיהֶֽם

verses.restored: From Zebulun: fifty thousand going out to battle, arraying with all weapons, keeping rank with undivided loyalty.

familiar.text: Of Zebulun, such as went forth to battle, expert in war, with all instruments of war, fifty thousand, which could keep rank: they were not of double heart.

modern.text: From Zebulun: 50,000 fit for service, trained for battle with all kinds of weapons of war, who with one purpose were devoted to David.

original.text: מִזְּבֻל֞וּן יוֹצְאֵ֣י צָבָ֗א עֹרְכֵ֧י מִלְחָמָ֛ה בְּכָל כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אָ֑לֶף וְלַעֲדֹ֖ר בְּלֹא לֵ֥ב וָלֵֽב

verses.restored: From Naphtali: one thousand commanders and thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.

familiar.text: And of Naphtali a thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty and seven thousand.

modern.text: From Naphtali: 1,000 commanders, accompanied by 37,000 men with shield and spear.

original.text: וּמִנַּפְתָּלִ֖י שָׂרִ֣ים אָ֑לֶף וְעִמָּהֶם֙ בְּצִנָּ֣ה וַחֲנִ֔ית שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף

verses.restored: From Dan: twenty-eight thousand six hundred trained for battle.

familiar.text: And of the Danites expert in war twenty and eight thousand and six hundred.

modern.text: From Dan: 28,600 prepared for battle.

original.text: וּמִן הַדָּנִי֙ עֹרְכֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִֽים וּשְׁמוֹנָ֥ה אֶ֖לֶף וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת

verses.restored: From Asher: forty thousand going out for battle and trained for war.

familiar.text: And of Asher, such as went forth to battle, expert in war, forty thousand.

modern.text: From Asher: 40,000 fit for service, prepared for battle.

original.text: וּמֵאָשֵׁ֗ר יוֹצְאֵ֥י צָבָ֛א לַעֲרֹ֥ךְ מִלְחָמָ֖ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים אָֽלֶף

verses.restored: From beyond Jordan—Reuben, Gad, half-Manasseh—with all battle weapons: one hundred twenty thousand.

familiar.text: And on the other side of Jordan, of the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and of the half tribe of Manasseh, with all manner of instruments of war for the battle, an hundred and twenty thousand.

modern.text: And from east of the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh there: 120,000 armed with every kind of weapon of war.

original.text: וּמֵעֵ֣בֶר לַ֠יַּרְדֵּן מִן הָראוּבֵנִ֨י וְהַגָּדִ֜י וַחֲצִ֣י שֵׁ֣בֶט מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה בְּכֹל֙ כְּלֵי֙ צְבָ֣א מִלְחָמָ֔ה מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָֽלֶף

verses.restored: All these warriors keeping rank came with whole heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; all rest of Israel were one heart to make David king, in idealized account.

familiar.text: All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.

modern.text: All these men of war, arrayed for battle, came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of the Israelites were of one mind to make David king.

original.text: כָּל אֵ֜לֶּה אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִלְחָמָה֮ עֹדְרֵ֣י מַעֲרָכָה֒ בְּלֵבָ֤ב שָׁלֵם֙ בָּ֣אוּ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת דָּוִ֖יד עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְ֠גַם כָּל שֵׁרִ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לֵ֥ב אֶחָ֖ד לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת דָּוִֽיד

verses.restored: They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for relatives prepared for them.

familiar.text: And there they were with David three days, eating and drinking: for their brethren had prepared for them.

modern.text: They spent three days there eating and drinking with David, for their relatives had provided for them.

original.text: וַיִּהְיוּ שָׁ֤ם עִם דָּוִיד֙ יָמִ֣ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֔ה אֹכְלִ֖ים וְשׁוֹתִ֑ים כִּֽי הֵכִ֥ינוּ לָהֶ֖ם אֲחֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Nearby people as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought bread on donkeys, camels, mules, oxen; food, flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance, for joy was in Israel.

familiar.text: Moreover they that were nigh them, even unto Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought bread on asses, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, and meat, meal, cakes of figs, and bunches of raisins, and wine, and oil, and oxen, and sheep abundantly: for there was joy in Israel.

modern.text: And their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali came bringing food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen—abundant supplies of flour, fig cakes and raisin cakes, wine and oil, oxen and sheep. Indeed, there was joy in Israel.

original.text: וְגַ֣ם הַקְּרֽוֹבִים אֲ֠לֵיהֶם עַד יִשָׂשכָ֨ר וּזְבֻל֜וּן וְנַפְתָּלִ֗י מְבִיאִ֣ים לֶ֡חֶם בַּחֲמוֹרִ֣ים וּבַגְּמַלִּ֣ים וּבַפְּרָדִ֣ים וּֽבַבָּקָ֡ר מַאֲכָ֡ל קֶ֠מַח דְּבֵלִ֨ים וְצִמּוּקִ֧ים וְיַֽיִן וְשֶׁ֛מֶן וּבָקָ֥ר וְצֹ֖אן לָרֹ֑ב כִּ֥י שִׂמְחָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

translation_notes: People joining David are defectors, refugees, kin of Saul, military professionals, and political actors with complex loyalties; they are not a simple unanimous movement.
Lion-face and gazelle-speed comparisons are warrior poetry, not body ideals or permission to animalize people.
Verse 15's valley flight implies harm and displacement beyond the celebrated river crossing.
David's claim of innocent hands must be tested against 1 Samuel, including his raids and deception from Ziklag.
Amasai's spirit-inspired declaration does not make political allegiance infallible or criticism of David unfaithful.
The Philistine commanders' rejection of David reflects specific wartime risk and may not justify profiling refugees or dual-loyalty minorities.
Troop numbers and command structures reflect militarization, not the total value or consent of each tribe.
Understanding the times in verse 32 is political discernment in context, not a warrant for authoritarian astrologers or secret-knowledge elites.
Idealized one-heart unity can erase dissent, women, noncombatants, Saul loyalists, and coerced participation.
The final feast depends on transport workers, farmers, bakers, animal labor, and regional supply chains.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to glorify defection, militarism, ethnic profiling, leader cults, forced unanimity, or obedience to spiritual-political elites. Preserve divided loyalties, civilian impact, logistical labor, and the right to question David's claimed innocence.
